elements.quote: Pulled from a wreck with no name. Some of the ink is still wet.

elements.p: I kept this book for thirty years at sea. Most of what is in it I saw with my own eyes. The rest I was told by men who did not live long after telling me.
The pages about the great beasts are blank until you are ready for them. Kill one, and the next one's page fills in by itself. I stopped asking why.

elements.quote: - the last captain to own it

elements.p: Before there were rings, the sea had two masters. THALASSAR, the Tide Father, drove the currents. The LEVIATHAN swallowed whatever the currents brought it.
They fought for an age. The Leviathan was stronger. So the old sea-folk did something terrible: they cut the heart out of Thalassar and sealed it, still beating, inside the ribs of a dead titan.
The Leviathan fears that heartbeat. While it beats, it sleeps.
A Keeper was left to guard the heart. Its tomb lies somewhere in the Maw Depths, far out at the edge of the world.
The Eye of Thalassar is still in there too, behind bars of bone. It watches.

elements.quote: "The heart is stone. The rift is open. It will wake hungry - and there is only ONE of it."

elements.p: The world is a set of rings around Wavebreak Port. The farther from port you sail, the older and worse the sea gets.

elements.row: I. The Starter Seas - shallows, thickets, open ocean
II. The Merchant Seas - coral and siren song
III. The Volcanic Seas - water that boils
IV. The Cursed Seas - shipwrecks and the drowned
V. The Abyss - the edge of the world

elements.p: A strange barrier keeps you out of the outer seas. Each boss you kill breaks the next seal. The Seas tab has more.
Wavebreak is the last safe harbour. It has piers and cranes, the Grog Barrel tavern, a chapel, a fort and a lighthouse.

Eight traders keep stalls around the fountain: Quartermaster, Fishmonger, Barkeep, Curio Dealer, Gunsmith, Chandler, Cook and the Map Merchant. Everyone here deals in doubloons. Pirate coin is pirate money - you take it off pirates, and only pirates want it.
The shipwright's drafting table is at the far end of the grand pier. Buy a ship there and it is built straight onto the water. Each captain may own one ship.
Four flags fly on these waters. Friends of one are often enemies of another. The Ship's Log tab shows where you stand with each.
Pirates. They attack anyone who isn't one of them.
Merchant ships full of cargo. They only fight back when attacked.
The navy. They hunt anyone who has made enemies of the law.
Dead crews on rotting hulls. You cannot bargain with them.
Take the helm to steer. Masts give speed, and more masts mean more speed. Ships have hull points and sink when those run out. A repair kit patches a hull at sea.
Click once to charge, again to fire. Aim high for range. Chain shot tears sails; grape shot sweeps decks.
Kill an enemy ship's captain and the ship is yours to plunder. A sunk ship stays afloat as a derelict for a few minutes before it goes down.
Every great beast leaves a relic behind. Each one protects you against the NEXT beast or its waters. Right-click a relic and it points the way to that beast's lair.
This book tells you about the world. Your Pirate Journal (J) tracks your level and skills.
